merger_description:
A consortium comprising:

* Zerra WDDP Investments Pte Ltd (**Zerra Singapore**) and Zerra WDDP HoldCo Pty Ltd as trustee for Zerra WDDP HoldCo Trust (**Zerra Australia**) (together, **Zerra**);
* Australian Data Centres – Mitchell Pty Ltd (**ADC**); and
* Macquarie DC Infrastructure Holdings Pty Limited (**Macquarie Company**) and Macquarie DC Infrastructure Pty Limited as trustee for Macquarie DC Infrastructure Trust (**Macquarie Trustee**) (together, **MacCap**)

proposes to acquire 100% of the shares in Wambo Cattle Company Pty Ltd (**WamboCo**) and the land owned by WamboCo, being Lots 1, 3, 5-8 and 11 on RP840794, Lot 125 on CPDY316 and Lot 118 on CPDY237 (the **Site**) (the **Acquisition**).

The Acquisition will occur through a special purpose vehicle, Wambo BidCo Pty Ltd (**BidCo**), which is controlled by the consortium. Zerra indirectly holds 50% of BidCo, while MacCap and ADC each indirectly hold 25%.

Following the Acquisition, the consortium intends to develop, finance, construct, own and operate a data centre campus on the Site.

Zerra Singapore is a Singapore-based investment vehicle of Zerra DC, and Zerra Australia is an Australian-based investment vehicle of Zerra DC. Zerra DC is a fully-integrated hyperscale data centre developer and operator serving leading cloud and AI businesses across Asia-Pacific.

ADC is an Australian private company that designs, builds and operates data centres and AI factories as digital infrastructure for government and critical infrastructure customers.

Macquarie Company is an Australian private company and holding subsidiary of Macquarie Group Limited and Macquarie Trustee is a subsidiary of Macquarie Group Limited. Macquarie Group Limited (ASX:MQG) is a global financial services group, offering asset management, finance, banking, advisory & risk and capital solutions services.

WamboCo is an Australian private company that owns and operates the Wambo feedlot, a beef cattle lot-feeding facility near Dalby, QLD.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition given:
a. while there is a very small horizontal overlap between the
consortium (and its connected entities) and WamboCo in the
supply of beef cattle feedlots in Australia, the parties’
combined share is low and there are several alternative
suppliers of beef cattle feedlots in Southern Queensland
b. the consortium (and its connected entities) does not
currently have any interests in data centres in Queensland,
there are several alternative suppliers of data centres in
Queensland (and Australia more broadly), and the
Acquisition does not appear likely to otherwise limit or
prevent competition from rivals
c. the Acquisition involves the consortium developing a new
data centre campus, which will not result in the removal of
an existing data centre.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
